roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Edmonds, WA?
roles.costP1: For an Edmonds home, budget $14–$26 per square foot installed — the tile, the setting materials, the prep and the labor all inside that number, with labor alone beginning at $11/sq ft. Tub-shower surrounds generally book at $3,200–$6,800; a complete bathroom — shower plus floor plus niche — most often lands from $6,500 to $14,000.
roles.costP2: A quiet truth of tile pricing: format drives labor harder than the sticker does. That little hex mosaic you love from 1962 takes many more cuts and joints than a modern large-format plank — which is why the modest tile sometimes carries the bigger install bill.
roles.costNote: Edmonds installed ranges, August 2026, with tile, materials and labor included. The written quote from the free visit is the number to trust.
roles.layersLead: A lasting shower is seven layers deep, and the order matters. When we open a failed one — including plenty of well-loved originals — the missing piece is almost always the membrane, skipped decades ago or last year to save a few hundred dollars.
roles.whyP1: Leaks announce themselves late. Water passes the grout line, settles into the substrate, and reveals itself years afterward — a floor that flexes, a shadow on the ceiling of the room below. The bill at that point covers framing, subfloor, drywall and a full re-tile.
roles.whyP2: Roughly a tenth of the shower's cost buys the waterproofing. Omitting it is the one economy that always comes back.
roles.scopeIntro: Opening prices. The tile you choose, the substrate we uncover and the layout you want each move them; the firm figure is put in writing on site, at no charge.
roles.cardShower: Built complete every time: a pre-sloped base under a bonded membrane, a flood test kept on record, then the niche, curb or curbless threshold, then tile. You're buying layers you'll never look at.
roles.cardFloors: Baths, kitchens, entries, mudrooms and daylight basements. Subfloors are flattened first; where the house moves or radiant heat is planned, an uncoupling membrane goes between.
roles.cardBacksplash: Subway, mosaic, herringbone or slab-look porcelain — including patterns that suit a mid-century kitchen. Clean outlet cuts, proper edge trim, grout matched to the counter.
roles.cardHeated: Electric radiant over an uncoupling membrane, resistance readings taken before and after the set, on its own dedicated circuit. It only pencils out while the floor is already up.
roles.cardRepair: Hairline cracks, tired grout, a corner pulling loose. We give you an honest read: a lasting repair, or a substrate that has already failed beneath the surface.
roles.cardDemo: Old tile, thinset and backer removed with the dust walled off behind sheeting and negative air. Everything is hauled away — nothing lingers at the curb.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Edmonds, WA?
roles.faqA1: In Edmonds, installed tile runs $14 to $26 per square foot once you include the tile, the setting materials, the prep and the labor; labor by itself opens at $11 per square foot. Budget $3,200–$6,800 for the standard tub-shower surround, and $6,500–$14,000 for a full bathroom holding floor, shower and niche. Note that format, not price, sets the labor: mosaic sheets and large-format tile each take meaningfully more work per square foot than 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Edmonds?
roles.faqA2: A standard alcove shower in Edmonds prices between $3,200 and $6,800, including demolition of the old surround, a bonded waterproofing system, the sloped base, the tile work, a niche and grout. Full-height stone, benches, steam and curbless entries carry premiums above that. The waterproofing is roughly ten percent of the bill — and the reason the rest of it lasts.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes — and that includes behind period-style tile. Each shower receives a bonded system following TCNA guidance: pre-sloped base, membrane brought wall-high in sheet or liquid form, corners, seams and penetrations all closed, and 24 hours of flood testing photographed ahead of tiling. The vintage character lives on the surface; the modern waterproofing lives behind it. Tile and grout never once kept framing dry alone.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is the usual Edmonds timeline. Day one covers demolition and dust walls; the next pairs substrate work with waterproofing, the 24-hour flood test close behind; setting occupies one or two; grout, silicone and trim finish it — then 24 quiet hours of curing before that first hot shower. A floor alone needs a day or two.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain for the working surfaces, ceramic where it's decorative. Porcelain's density — under 0.5% water absorption — and chip resistance make it right for floors, shower floors and wet areas. Ceramic is more affordable and perfectly good on walls and backsplashes, which is also where a vintage-style ceramic can carry an Edmonds bathroom's character. Every floor we spec is porcelain.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — quietly, under the tile, without changing the room's face. Figure $11 to $16 per installed square foot, thermostat included. The mat installs over an uncoupling membrane, gets resistance readings before and after setting, and runs on a dedicated circuit. It only makes sense while the floor is already up; in a remodel, that's exactly when we are.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Almost always — especially with 60-year-old floors, where the mud bed underneath tells the real story. Removal and haul-away is around $3.50 per square foot and gives us the subfloor in plain view: rot, movement, and the transition heights at each doorway. Over-tiling works only on a flat, sound, well-bonded floor, and even then it raises the level and hides history. We'd rather see it.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Edmonds?
roles.faqA8: Edmonds kitchens usually pay $1,100–$2,200 for a 30-square-foot backsplash installed — outlet cuts, finished edges and grout picked against the countertop included. Layout and cutting hours explain the top half: mosaic sheets, herringbone, a picture-framed panel at the range, slab-look porcelain climbing to the ceiling. Straight-set subway keeps you at the calmer end.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often — and with original tile worth preserving, repair is where we start the conversation. Starting at $8 per square foot, we renew stained or failing grout joints, swap impact-cracked tiles, and redo shower corners in silicone. The limit is substrate failure: hollow sounds, tiles loosening in a pattern, a wall with give. There a repair buys months only, and we'll tell you so plainly before quoting either path.
roles.faqQ10: Which Edmonds neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Edmonds — Seaview, the Bowl, Westgate, Perrinville, Five Corners, Firdale, Sherwood Forest, Maplewood, Meadowdale, Talbot Park, Lake Ballinger, Point Edwards, Chase Lake, Emerald Hills and Esperance — plus Woodway, Mountlake Terrace, Shoreline, Lynnwood, Mukilteo and the neighboring shoreline communities.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every tile install comes with a 2-year workmanship warranty — tile earns a longer term than carpet from us because its failures announce themselves slowly. Put in a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly and the maker's coverage joins ours. Membranes and flood tests get photographed without exception, handing an Edmonds house with three careful owners one more documented chapter.
